1. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned counsel for the respondents.
2.

The present writ petition has been filed for the following relief :-
(a) For issuance of a writ in the nature of mandamus commanding upon the respondents specially Respondent No.3 to make payment with statutory interest till its actual payment of compensation at the present market rate which has been paid to the petitioner in land Acquisition Case No.22/ 2012-13 against the Award No.183 Ashwani Kumar Gupta vs The State Of Jharkhand on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109497163/
1 prepared for the purpose of widening of NH-02 with respect to Rs.17,59,292.00/-
against the land which has been acquired by the respondents.
3. It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that though the petitioners have received compensation of Rs.17,59,292/- under protest pursuant to Award No.183 prepared in connection with Land Acquisition Case No. 22/2012-13, however, they have not been paid any amount for the house situated over the said land.

entities.text: Ashwani Kumar Gupta vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Moreover, the said compensation was also paid to them at the old rate.

The petitioners raised the objection before the respondent No.3 in this regard,
however, no action has been taken, which has compelled them to prefer the present writ petition.

4. It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the respondent/ NHAI that the petitioners have got statutory/ efficacious remedy under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act, 1956') for redressal of their grievance.
5. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and from the materials available on record, it appears that the petitioners have got statutory/ efficacious remedy under Section 3G(5) of the Act,
1956 for ventilating his grievance and as such, without going into the merit of the case, they are given liberty to prefer an application raising the objection with regard to insufficient payment of compensation to them in connection with Land Acquisition Case No.22/2012-13 before the respondent No.3.
On receipt of the said representation, the respondent No.3 shall refer the matter to the Additional Collector, Hazaribagh -cum- Arbitrator under the provisions of Section 3G(5) of the Act, 1956 within 30 days from the date of receipt of the said application.
6.
Accordingly, the present writ petition is hereby, disposed of with the aforesaid liberty and direction.

(Rajesh Kumar, J.) Chandan/-
